messages:
devon: FYI — saw a regression after the latest runtime rollout. prefix/KV cache hit-rate dropped ~28% for short-seq traffic (<=64) and P95 gen latency +12ms. digging in now. :eyes:
ana: Can you paste the aggregate numbers and any profiler traces you have?
devon: quick snippet from prod metrics (last 30m):
```
cache_requests: 54,321
cache_hits: 39,112
hit_rate: 72.0%  <-- was ~100% in last stable window
evictions/sec: 18
avg_kv_size_per_gpu: 1.2MB
```
lucy: Interesting. Did anything change to keying logic in recent PRs? I vaguely remember #452 touched prompt trimming.
devon: good call — PR #452 normalized trailing whitespace and removed some punctuation when building the prefix key. Might have increased key cardinality.
sahil: Also check autoscaler churn. If we scale down GPUs aggressively they flush local KV caches. Any scale events coincident with the drop?
opsbot: autoscaler: scale_down event at 1792554290 -> 2 nodes removed, grace=30s.
devon: timeline matches. scale_down at ~1792554290 then hit-rate crater. so two factors: key canon changes + node churn.
lucy: That explains it. Two obvious mitigations: 1) warm caches after deploy/scale events, 2) revert key normalization if it added noise. But revert is risky.
ana: Proposal: hybrid preseed strategy — small deploy-time seeder job that preloads top-N hot prefixes, plus an autoscale hook that triggers a fast synthetic burst (local-only) to populate local KV for each restarted GPU. Keep synthetic burst size tiny to avoid cost.
sahil: +1. Also add a short-term scheduled job: run cheap seeding every 3h to catch slowly drifting hot prefixes. For keying, we should compute a stable shard key by hashing a normalized form (lowercase + collapse spaces) rather than removing punctuation heuristically.
devon: rough seeder command we ran for experiments:
```bash
kubectl run cache-seeder --restart=OnFailure --image=redwood/cache-tools:canary -- 
  --seed-list /mnt/hot_prefixes.txt --parallelism 8 --target-gpus all
```
This job warmed ~95% of top-100 prefixes within 30s.
lucy: Nice. Questions: 1) where do we keep hot_prefixes.txt? 2) how do we ensure seeder runs after node join and not too early?
ana: Answers: 1) S3 artifact generated by analytics job (daily top-k). 2) Use autoscaler hook: when node becomes Ready, run a DaemonJob on that node (k8s node lifecycle hook) or ephemeral sidecar that requests the seed file and executes local seeding.
sahil: Caveat: for strict isolation (Dedicated/Private), we might not have S3 access. For those customers run seeding from inside their VPC or package the top-k in the release artifact.
devon: Also we should be careful about synthetic traffic affecting our metrics or billing. Tag seeding requests with header `x-internal-seed: 1` and exclude from billing and eval alerts.
lucy: Operational metrics to add to dashboards: `prefix_cache.hit_rate_by_node`, `prefix_cache.evictions`, `seeder.job_duration`, `seeder.requests_tagged`, and `prefix_key_cardinality_daily`.
opsbot: note: added `prefix_cache.hit_rate_by_node` to the eng-runtime grafana folder.
ana: Rollout plan suggestion:
- canary 10% with deploy-seeder enabled + autoscale hook (24h)
- monitor hit-rate, P95, evictions. If stable, expand to 50% then 100%.
- scheduled seeder job every 6h for first week then adapt cadence.
sahil: Also add a microbenchmark to our perf CI that simulates scale-in/out and measures seed-recovery time. We saw recovery to steady-state took ~7 minutes without seeding. With seeder it was ~40s.
devon: I'll open two tickets: one for implementing autoscaler hook + seeder job, one to refactor key generation to deterministic hash-normalize.
lucy: I'll own the canary and metrics. ana, can you coordinate with infra to add the node lifecycle hook?
ana: Yep — will spin up infra PR and also ensure seeding requests are tagged.
deploy-bot: deploy job queued: infra/autohook-seeder -> review required.
devon: TL;DR: regression caused by increased key cardinality + scale churn. Short-term mitigation: deploy lightweight seeder + autoscale hook + tag seed traffic. Longer-term: stabilize keying and add seeding to CI. Action owners assigned. :thumbsup:
